Hi Jenna / Alex —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for taking the time to walk through your current inference/observability setup. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights:
- Current pain: high tail latency variability during peak traffic and difficulty attributing cost to lines of business.
- What you liked about Redwood: unified runtime, built-in tracing for token-level latency attribution, and the model-variant fallback for reliability.
- Primary comparison points vs hyperscalers you asked about: observability detail (tracing/metrics granularity), retention/ingestion, export integrations (Datadog/Prometheus), and cost attribution per route.

What we can provide immediately (attachments):
- redwood-product-one-pager.pdf — high-level features and observability components.
- evaluation-plan.xlsx — suggested spike plan: 1) ingest sample traffic, 2) run 48h load window w/ synthetic peaks, 3) compare latency percentiles, KV cache hit rates, and cost per token.

1) Minimum sample traffic profile (qps and sequence length distribution) — can you share a 48h sample?
2) Any security/compliance gating (IP allowlist, subnets, or special data handling) for a private evaluation?

Proposed next steps:
- You share the 48h traffic sample + any compliance constraints (reply to this thread).
- Schedule a 45-min technical deep dive next week (I proposed 4 slots in the calendar invite).
- We’ll prepare a short eval runbook and a Datadog dashboard template to mirror what you’ll see in production.

If that sounds good I’ll kick off the Eval plan and loop infra to set up the test cluster.

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our infra team before we send the sample: 

- Tracing granularity: Can Redwood provide spans down to model-call/token granularity? We currently send traces at the request level and correlate to model IDs — for us token-level visibility would be ideal to debug generation-level regressions.
- Retention: We keep metrics for 90 days and traces for 30 days on our side. What retention windows do you offer for traces/metrics and are there tiered options?
- Integrations: We use Datadog + S3 for cold storage. We’d need logs/metrics exported to Datadog and long-term artifacts to S3. Any known limitations here?

Also curious about the hyperscaler comparison — you mentioned automated fallback to cheaper model variants. How is cost attribution reported when a request is routed to a fallback model?

Will share the 48h sample tomorrow. One more ask: can you share the evaluation-plan.xlsx ahead of the scheduling so our security reviewer can glance?

Best,

Hey Jenna — happy to weigh in. Short answers to your infra questions: 

- Token-level tracing: Yes — Redwood includes optional token-level spans when you enable the tracing hook. We capture model-init, forward-token, and KV cache hit events. By default token spans are sampled at 1% for high-throughput workloads but can be increased to 100% for short eval windows.
- Retention: Platform defaults are metrics 90d, traces 30d. We offer add-on retention (180/365d) and can export raw traces to S3 for long-term archival.
- Datadog integration: We provide a Metrics -> Datadog exporter and ship trace spans via OpenTelemetry. Dashboards are templated — you’ll get percentiles (P50/P90/P99) per model route, KV cache hit ratio, burst latency heatmaps, and per-caller cost attribution charts.

About fallback cost attribution: when a request is routed to a fallback model variant we record both the original route intent and the executed model in the event. Our billing/attribution pipeline attaches executed-model tags so you can filter cost by intended route or by actual execution. The evaluation-plan.xlsx includes an example breakdown for mixed routing.

I’m attaching the evaluation plan and a short dashboard screenshot (in the Drive folder) — taking Rishi off-list for any contract/pricing questions but cc’d here since he’ll own the pricing side after the spike.

— Logan
